title: Young-Driver Surcharge Rates on Longer Keyturn Trip Booking Reserved Periods
content:
On a Keyturn Trip Booking whose reserved period runs for 14 days or more, the young-driver surcharge rate depends on whether a deposit line stands on the reservation.

1. Where the reserved period runs for 14 days or more and a deposit line stands on the reservation, whatever was afterwards done about it, the surcharge rate is 9 per cent.
2. Where the reserved period runs for 14 days or more and no deposit line stands on the reservation, the surcharge rate is 18 per cent.
3. In every other case the surcharge rate is the standard one.

### The rule as a table

| Length of the reserved period | Deposit line standing on the reservation | Surcharge rate |
|---|---|---|
| 14 days or more | One or more, whatever was afterwards done about it | 9 per cent |
| 14 days or more | None | 18 per cent |
| Fewer than 14 days | One or more | The standard one |
| Fewer than 14 days | None | The standard one |

The days of the reserved period are counted from the first day of that period to the last, both days counted. Fourteen days is reached rather than passed: a reserved period of exactly 14 days sits in the first or second row, one of 13 days in the third or fourth.

Whether a deposit line stands is read from the priced lines raised against the reservation, and such a line counts whatever was afterwards done about it, so a deposit since released, refunded or reversed counts just as one still held does. One such line is enough; the amount it was raised for makes no difference to which row governs.

*Hypothetical.* A reserved period of 21 days on which a deposit line stands takes a surcharge rate of 9 per cent, and it still takes 9 per cent where that deposit was afterwards released in full. The same reserved period with no deposit line ever raised takes 18 per cent — the rate on an unsecured long reservation being the highest of the three. A reserved period of 6 days takes the standard rate whether or not a deposit line stands on it.
